newsitem.title: UK: UK background inflation pressures still dormant.
newsitem.headline: UK background inflation pressures still dormant.

text.p: Prices of goods leaving British factories were steady in July, the government said Monday, indicating inflation remained under control.
The Office for National Statistics said output prices rose just 0.2 percent in July, leaving them just 1.4 percent higher than a year ago.
The cost of raw materials paid by Britain's manufacturers dropped a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent on the month and were a significant 9 percent lower than in July last year.
Economists said the meteoric rise in the value of the pound -- it spurted another 4 percent higher in July -- was keeping inflation pressures well under control.

"The strength of sterling is killing input prices at the moment while the strength of domestic demand is allowing output prices to creep up," said Robin Marshall, chief economist at Chase Investment Bank. "At the moment, sterling is winning out overall."
The Bank of England raised interest rates for the fourth time in as many months last week, but hinted that it would be the last tightening for some time.
"It's not producer prices that is worrying the Bank of England, it's the pace of consumer demand," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
